phenotypes: complete transposition of the great arteries
right-sided aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery
WAGR syndrome (2 patients; 1 with normal cardiac findings, 1 with insufficient cardiac information)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Known germline WT1 mutations or 11p13 deletions in children with Wilms' tumor; retrospective review suggests an increased incidence of congenital heart defects.
clinical.center_country: The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, Canada

model_organism.knockout_type: conditional knockout (forebrain-specific WT1-deficient mice) plus hippocampal knockdown
phenotypes: WT1 knockdown enhanced CA1 neuronal excitability, LTP and long-term memory
Forebrain WT1-deficient mice showed deficits in reversal learning and sequential learning tasks
Impaired contextual fear extinction, indicating impaired memory flexibility

model_organism.citation: WT1 directs normal progesterone receptor-chromatin binding essential for uterine receptivity at peri-implantation (PMID: 40627402)
phenotypes: Attenuated progesterone responsiveness in uterine stromal cells
Impaired PR-chromatin binding and reduced transcription of PR target genes

model_organism.citation: Activation of podocyte Notch mediates early Wt1 glomerulopathy (PMID: 29398135)
model_organism.knockout_type: conditional knockout (tamoxifen-inducible Cre-loxP deletion of Wt1 in adult mice)
phenotypes: Podocyte Notch activation (Notch1, Nrarp, Hey2, HES1 upregulated)
Notch inhibition ameliorated glomerular scarring and albuminuria

model_organism.citation: Alternatively spliced isoforms of WT1 control podocyte-specific gene expression (PMID: 25993318)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (mice lacking the WT1 +KTS splice isoform)
phenotypes: A restricted set of genes was dependent on the +KTS isoform, including MAGI2
MAGI2α is needed for nephrin localization and slit diaphragm assembly
Reduced MAGI2 in LPS glomerular injury model

model_organism.citation: Wt1 transcription factor impairs cardiomyocyte specification and drives a phenotypic switch from myocardium to epicardium (PMID: 35312773)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (ectopic/sustained wt1a and wt1b overexpression in cardiomyocytes; gain-of-function, not knockout)
phenotypes: Sustained wt1b expression reduced chromatin accessibility
Cardiomyocytes delaminated from the myocardium and upregulated epicardial genes

model_organism.citation: Dose-Dependent and Non-Autonomous Signaling in CAKUT: A Lineage-Specific Framework from Conditional Knockout Studies (PMID: 41897393)
model_organism.knockout_type: conditional knockout (Six2-Cre-mediated Wt1 deletion in nephron progenitors; review)
phenotypes: Pro-apoptotic phenotype with loss of Wt1, rescued by exogenous FGF
Loss of Wt1 impairs FGF signaling and increases BMP/pSMAD activity

biological.citation: Autophagy regulates differentiation of ovarian granulosa cells through degradation of WT1 (PMID: 35025698)
biological.summary: siRNA knockdown of ATG5 or BECN1, or chloroquine treatment, in granulosa cells caused WT1 to accumulate because autophagic degradation was insufficient. This reduced CYP19A1 and FSHR expression and estradiol synthesis. GCs from biochemical POI patients showed reduced autophagy markers.

biological.citation: Epg5 deficiency leads to primary ovarian insufficiency due to WT1 accumulation in mouse granulosa cells (PMID: 35786405)
biological.summary: Epg5 knockout mice showed a POI-like phenotype with blocked autophagic flux. WT1 accumulated in granulosa cells, which reduced steroidogenesis-related gene expression and impaired GC differentiation, indicating WT1 is selectively degraded by autophagy via EPG5.

biological.citation: Inhibition of transcriptional coactivator YAP Impairs the expression and function of transcription factor WT1 in diabetic podocyte injury (PMID: 38423183)
biological.summary: Podocyte-specific Yap knockout in diabetic mice decreased WT1 expression and the expression of WT1 targets, including Tead1. This places WT1 downstream of Hippo/YAP signaling in diabetic podocyte injury.

biological.citation: TERT Expression in Wilms Tumor Is Regulated by Promoter Mutation or Hypermethylation, WT1, and N-MYC (PMID: 35406427)
biological.summary: WTs with biallelic WT1 inactivating mutations (7/45) had lower TERT expression and telomerase activity. WT1 shRNA knockdown in WiT49 cells decreased TERT, colony formation and proliferation. An inducible Wt1 knockout in normal mouse nephrogenesis showed no effect on Tert, so the WT1-TERT coupling appears specific to transformed cells.

biological.citation: WT1 recruits TET2 to regulate its target gene expression and suppress leukemia cell proliferation (PMID: 25601757)
biological.summary: WT1 physically interacts with TET2 and recruits it to WT1 target genes to activate their expression. WT1 mutations are mutually exclusive with TET2/IDH1/IDH2 mutations in AML. AML-derived TET2 mutations disrupt the interaction, and TET2 suppression of leukemia cell proliferation depends on WT1.

biological.citation: Alternatively spliced isoforms of WT1 control podocyte-specific gene expression (PMID: 25993318)
biological.summary: ChIP-seq showed that almost half of podocyte-specific genes are direct WT1 targets, with FOXC1 binding sites near WT1-bound regions. Mice lacking the +KTS isoform showed altered expression of a restricted gene set including MAGI2, which is needed for nephrin localization and slit diaphragm assembly.

biological.citation: WT1 and its transcriptional cofactor BASP1 redirect the differentiation pathway of an established blood cell line (PMID: 21269271)
biological.summary: BASP1 is recruited to WT1-binding sites and suppresses WT1-mediated transcriptional activation. In K562 cells, WT1 and BASP1 together diverted PMA-induced differentiation to a neuronal-like phenotype.

biological.citation: Antagonistic activities of CDC14B and CDK1 on USP9X regulate WT1-dependent mitotic transcription and survival (PMID: 32152317)
biological.summary: WT1 was identified as a substrate that is deubiquitylated and stabilized by CDK1-phosphorylated USP9X (S2563) in mitosis. WT1 acts as a mitotic transcription factor and drives expression of its target CXCL8/IL-8, which conveys mitotic survival. CDC14B antagonizes this pathway.

biological.citation: Classification of a frameshift/extended and a stop mutation in WT1 as gain-of-function mutations that activate cell cycle genes and promote Wilms tumour cell proliferation (PMID: 24619359)
biological.summary: In Wilms tumour cell lines, mutant WT1 (p.V432fsX87 and p.P362X) showed gain-of-function activity. It upregulated G2/M cell cycle genes needed for proliferation, interacted physically with p53, and antagonized p53-mediated repression.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Pleiotropic effects of noncoding variants near EFEMP1, WT1, ADAMTS6, and EBF2 on the risk of abdominal hernias
biological.summary: Noncoding variants at the WT1 locus were associated with inguinal hernia risk and with umbilical, femoral and ventral hernias. WT1 is expressed in mouse connective tissue, and pathway analysis suggests it influences connective tissue homeostasis through extracellular matrix enzymes such as MMPs.
